title: unblock-prs configuration
description: What a repository says about itself in .github/unblock-prs.json: the parts of an unblock-prs run that depend on how its CI is laid out, and the branches it generates. Labels, Merge-After: and the version pull request's branch are fixed conventions, not set here.

autoFix.description: How to fix a failure that is only a fixer's diff: a job whose clean-tree check fails once its command has run. Absent: a failure is never fixed, only reported.

ignore.description: Regular expressions for failed contexts that are only the echo of another, such as an aggregate job, and are not read.

before.description: Commands run first, always: what CI does before any job (an install).

prepare.description: Commands run after `before` when a context being fixed matches `context`, each command once: what CI gives some jobs and not others (a build).

fixers.description: Every failed context not ignored has to match one of these, the first that matches deciding, or nothing is fixed.

context.description: A regular expression for the failed context's name.

run.description: The command, where $1 to $9 are the context's capture groups, shell-quoted.

stage.description: Lower stages run first, and within a stage by command.

after.description: Commands run last, always: settling what the fixers wrote (a formatter).

notFixableAnnotation.description: The title of an annotation a job leaves on its check run when its command failed, rather than only leaving a diff: such a context is declined at planning, without an install. For a job that runs its command and its clean-tree check in one step, whose steps cannot say which failed. Absent: every failed context matching a fixer is tried.

regenerate.description: How to resolve a rebase whose conflicts are all in generated files: take the base's side of each, finish the rebase, run `before` and the generators, and amend what they wrote onto the pull request's one commit. A file the generators leave as the base has it, though the pull request changed it, stops this: the generator did not reproduce the pull request's side. Absent: every conflict is set aside, as it is when any conflicted file is not generated.

before.description: Commands run first, before any generator: what the generators need (an install).

generators.description: The first whose `path` matches a conflicted file decides how it is written again; a conflicted file none matches is resolved by hand.

path.description: A regular expression for a path, from the repository root, that the command writes whole.

run.description: The command that writes it, where $1 to $9 are the path's capture groups, shell-quoted.

generatedBranches.description: Branches the repository generates whole, lockfile and all, such as a dependency update. A conflict on one is resolved by building it again, never by a rebase resolved by hand: push-fixed-pr refuses that push, and the skill runs `rebuild` instead.

branch.description: The pull request's head branch, exactly.

rebuild.description: How the branch is built again from the tip of the default branch, as a person or the skill would run it; push-fixed-pr names it when it refuses.

speculate.description: Check queued pull requests ahead of their turn: the leading ones are stacked on the default branch, one commit each, each on a `queue/pr-<number>` branch, and the workflows are dispatched on each with `diff-parent`. A pull request is released once its layer is green, and the gate reuses that verdict. Absent: one pull request is checked at a time.

workflows.description: The file names of the check workflows to dispatch on each layer, such as `code-check.yml`: every workflow that reports a required context. Each takes the `diff-parent` input.

depth.description: How many queued pull requests are stacked and checked ahead at most, the first included.

translation.description: Pull request and issue descriptions are written twice: the original, which tools and sessions read, then its translation under one `## <heading>`, its headings one level down, ending at the first `---` rule. Present: `open-pr --body-file` and `pr-description push` / `create` refuse a body whose halves do not mirror each other, and `pr-description read` leaves the translation out. Absent: descriptions are taken as they are.

heading.description: The text of the `## ` heading the translation follows the original under, such as `日本語`.
